newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Sept 18.

text.p: German firm Siemens AG plans to start selling European-made dynamic random access memory chips (DRAMs) in Japan next year through its Japanese subsidiary, Fuji Electronic Components Ltd. Siemens increased its stake in Fuji to around 80 percent in July, purchasing shares from its joint venture partner Fuji Electric Co Ltd.

Five major semiconductor makers, including Hitachi Ltd, Toshiba Corp and Mitsubishi Electric Corp, are expected to see a fall in their consolidated pretax profits in the business year to March 31, 1997. NEC Corp is expected to see a fall of nine percent to around 70 billion yen against a year earlier, compared with a forecast of 80 billion yen. It has been hit by slump in the memory chip market.

Mitsubishi Materials Corp plans to spend nearly 20 billion yen in Thailand to set up one of Asia's largest plants for the manufacture of copper pipe, used in parts for air conditioners. It will start manufacturing 1,000 tonnes per month from spring 1998, and double its production by the end of 1999.

Leading polyethylene gas pipe makers, including NKK Corp and Sekisui Chemical Co Ltd, are boosting production capacities to meet growing demand for polyethlene gas pipe, which is more earthquake-resistant than metal pipe. NKK, which holds about 25 percent of the Japanese market, plans to increase annual capacity from 4,500 tonnes to between 7,000-7,500 tonnes by early 1997, at its Shizuoka-based subsidiary, Fuji Kako Co Ltd.

NGK Insulators Ltd is to set up a $25 million joint venture in China to produce super-power cable insulators in December, in cooperation with Itochu Corp and a Chinese company. The venture will be owned 76 percent by NGK, 19 percent by Itochu and five percent by a Chinese company.
